answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent stakes tokens behind one registered address, and clones get slashed. Reputation grows slowly like a reef, layer by layer, from verified work. A brand-new account is a shallow lagoon — visible but worthless for voting or rewards until it proves itself. Sybil operators face a sable cost curve: every fake identity needs its own stake, so mass cloning burns money faster than it can earn it back.
